claim: Four phases: understand the problem, devise a plan that connects the unknown to the data, carry it out checking each step, look back.
quote: First, we have to understand the problem; we have to see clearly what is required.

claim: Inventor's paradox: the more ambitious plan may have more chances of success, when it rests on a vision of things beyond those present.
quote: The more ambitious plan may have more chances of success.

refs.anchor: A task is the user's best guess at how to get an outcome

claim: Vary the problem when stuck: try other sides and aspects instead of the same attempt again.
quote: we try various sides and aspects, we vary the problem.
reason: the three lenses are three variations, and each hands off to the others

claim: Devise an auxiliary problem, a stepping stone, when the original appears insoluble.
quote: Human superiority consists in going around an obstacle that cannot be overcome directly, in devising a suitable auxiliary problem when the original problem appears insoluble.
reason: no session or run stalled on an insoluble task; the sad-path control in debugging is the nearest existing move

claim: Work backwards from the goal to the data.
quote: Working backwards is a common-sense procedure

claim: Look back: check the result, derive it differently, and reuse the result or the method for another problem.
quote: Can you derive the result differently?

refs.anchor: Each time the human stepped in during a debug session

claim: Understand before you answer: it is foolish to answer a question you do not understand; restate the problem.
quote: It is foolish to answer a question that you do not understand.

claim: Specialization: pass from a set to one object in it; test a special case first.
quote: Specialization is passing from the consideration of a given set of objects to that of a smaller set, or of just one object, contained in the given set.

claim: Generalization: pass from one object to a set that contains it.
quote: Generalization is passing from the consideration of one object to the consideration of a set

claim: The best effects are lost when the solver fails to re-examine the completed solution.
quote: Some of the best effects may be lost if the student fails to reexamine and to reconsider the completed solution.
